invariants.admin_authority: HTTP supplies bounded bytes and a host-observed channel binding; HP4 alone owns authenticated entry, replay, command acceptance, terminal, audit, update, and recovery
invariants.admin_reserve: application routes cannot register in the admin namespace or occupy the independent admin HTTPS server, parser, or socket reserve
invariants.app_authority: a registered route dispatches one bounded HTTP event through the common Wasm handler and admits at most one first-response-wins paired effect
invariants.boot_authority: HP3 remains the sole durable application-slot, last-confirmed, trial, fallback, and reboot-selection authority
invariants.client_loss: network loss is counted and tears down the transport response only; it does not roll back an application or cancel an accepted HP4 command
invariants.credentials: Wi-Fi credentials, certificate and private-key pointers, sockets, reconnect policy, and TLS state remain host-private
invariants.failure_order: malformed, oversized, slow, disconnected, unauthorized, stale, replayed, and saturated input rejects before HP4 command acceptance mutation
invariants.resource_authority: HP1 scheduling, administration/recovery lanes, fixed reserve, and exclusive update admission are unchanged

routes.registration: exact GET or POST routes only; immutable after service start
